hints.content:
$g$ is increasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $g(x)$ also increases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going upwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by four. The graph of y equals g of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through the point negative five, twelve and it increases to the local maximum at three, fourteen. Then it decreases through the point negative one, twelve, the y-intercept zero, ten, and the point one, six. It continues to decrease through the x-intercept two and one-half zero and the point four, negative ten. All values are estimated. The function is highlighted from x equals negative five to x equals negative three.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $g$ increasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-3<x<-2$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $g$ is decreasing on this interval
$-1<x<0$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $g$ is decreasing on this interval
$2<x<3$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $g$ is decreasing on this interval

Therefore, $g$ is increasing on none of the above intervals.
